title: Seller's Residential Real Estate Sales Disclosure
description: Indiana Code §32-21-5-7 requires the owner of residential real estate to complete and deliver the Seller's Residential Real Estate Sales Disclosure form to the buyer before an offer is accepted. The form covers 21 categories including structural, mechanical, environmental conditions, and known defects. Applies to 1-4 unit residential properties with certain exemptions (IC §32-21-5-3).

required_actions.note: Must be completed and provided before acceptance of offer. State-approved form required (Indiana Real Estate Commission form).

title: Agency Disclosure and Duties
description: Indiana Code §25-34.1-10-9.5 requires licensees to provide a written disclosure of agency duties at the first substantive contact. Indiana recognizes buyer's agents, seller's agents, limited agents (dual agency), and transaction brokers. Dual agency (limited agency) requires written informed consent from both parties.

required_actions.note: Written disclosure of agency duties required at first substantive contact. Limited agency (dual agency) requires written consent.

title: Title Company Closing State
description: Indiana is a title company closing state. Closings are typically handled by title companies. Attorney presence is not required by statute for residential closings. Title insurance is standard practice.

required_actions.note: Title companies handle closings. Attorney optional but recommended for complex transactions.

title: Radon Disclosure and Testing Notice
description: Indiana's seller disclosure form (IC §32-21-5-7) includes a specific radon disclosure section. Indiana has significant radon risk, particularly in the northern and central counties. Sellers must disclose known radon test results and any radon mitigation systems installed. The Indiana State Department of Health maintains radon zone maps classifying all 92 counties.

required_actions.note: Seller must disclose known radon test results and any mitigation systems on the statutory disclosure form.
EPA recommends mitigation if radon levels exceed 4.0 pCi/L.

title: Flood Plain and Drainage Disclosure
description: Indiana's seller disclosure form requires disclosure of whether the property is in a FEMA-designated flood zone, whether the property has experienced flooding or drainage problems, and whether flood insurance has been required. Indiana DNR maintains floodplain maps and the Flood Control Act (IC §14-28-1) governs flood plain management.

required_actions.note: Flood zone status and flooding history must be disclosed on the statutory seller disclosure form.
Lenders require flood insurance for properties in FEMA SFHA zones.
